articles.title: He Took ‘Zealous Advocacy’ A Fatal Step Too Far
articles.content:
**《每日冷知识》**

哪位19世纪著名律师——同时也是内战时期最臭名昭著的政治家之一——因在为一名谋杀嫌疑犯辩护时提出被害者是因从口袋中快速拔枪导致意外走火而身亡的说法而闻名？为了证明这点，他用一把他认为没有装弹的枪重现了现场。然而，枪里有子弹。他自杀了，第二天去世。尽管他自己因此丧命，但他的当事人却因此获罪。

**提示**：在这次惨烈的示范之前，他曾是俄亥俄州的国会议员，也是反战“铜头蛇派”民主党的领袖——以至于林肯总统在1863年将他流放到南方联盟。
articles.summary:
Ed. Note: Welcome to our daily feature Trivia Question of the Day!

Which prominent 19th-century lawyer — and one of the most notorious politicians of the Civil War era — was defending a man accused of murder, arguing that the victim had actually shot himself by accident while yanking his own pistol from his pocket. To prove it, the lawyer reenacted the scene with a gun he believed was unloaded. It wasn’t. He shot himself and died the next day — but he won his client an acquittal.

Hint: Before this grisly demonstration, he’d been an Ohio congressman and the leader of the anti-war “Copperhead” Democrats — so troublesome to the Union that President Lincoln had him exiled to the Confederacy in 1863.

The post He Took ‘Zealous Advocacy’ A Fatal Step Too Far appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: The 3 Things Every Healthy Organization Needs
articles.content:
在与咨询师兼作家Cheryl Donaldson的近期对话中，我们探讨了一个法律事务所无法忽视的挑战：年轻有才华的律师比以往任何时候都更愿意因为不合适的企业文化而离职。

Cheryl带来了超过三十年的临床经验，以及心理学家对是什么真正让员工留下来、发展并成长，以及是什么默默驱使他们离开的清晰见解。

**健康组织的需求**
Cheryl构建员工愿意留下的企业的框架归结为三个不可或缺的要素。缺少其中任何一个，情况就会开始恶化。

**失而复得**
Cheryl在节目中最直接的观察之一是关于混合办公和远程办公转变中默默丢失的东西。当员工感觉自己像是生产线上的工人而非团队成员时，他们会选择离开。这种联系必须有意创造，否则人才就会流失。

**非线性发展**
Cheryl对关于她最大失误的问题的回答，是节目中最具启发性的时刻之一。她传递并带给她合作的律师和领导者的教训是，非线性发展时刻并非偏离方向，往往正是真正成长发生的地方。

Steve Fretzin是五次《纽约时报》畅销书作者，主持《BE THAT LAWYER》和《未来雨露者》播客，也是一位专为律师服务的业务发展教练。在过去18年中，他帮助律师通过不卖、不推销、不追逐的无销售销售™方法建立强大的客户群。他的客户经常成为顶级雨露者，并将其成功归功于他的培训和系统。可以通过电子邮件steve@fretzin.com或网站www.bethatlawyer.com直接联系Steve。在LinkedIn上与他联系：https://www.linkedin.com/in/stevefretzin。他的全新《BE THAT LAWYER》社区正在改变律师开发法学院从未教授过的技能的方式。了解更多：www.bethatlawyer.com/community。

原文标题：The 3 Things Every Healthy Organization Needs
首发于：Above the Law
articles.summary:
In a recent conversation with consultant and author Cheryl Donaldson, I explored a challenge that is becoming impossible for law firms to ignore: young, talented lawyers are more willing than ever to walk out the door if the culture doesn’t work for them.

What Cheryl brought to the conversation was over three decades of clinical experience and a psychologist’s clarity about what actually makes people stay, thrive, and grow inside an organization, and what quietly drives them away.

What Healthy Organizations Need

Cheryl’s framework for building a firm people want to stay in comes down to three non-negotiables. When any one of the three is missing, things start to unravel.

Hiding in Plain Sight

One of the most direct observations Cheryl made in the episode was about what has quietly been lost in the shift to hybrid and remote work.

When people feel like they’re part of an assembly line rather than a team, they leave. The connection has to be created intentionally, or the talent walks.

The Non-Linear Path

Cheryl’s answer to the closing question about her biggest mistake was one of the most grounding moments of the episode.

The lesson she carried forward, and the one she brings to the lawyers and leaders she works with, is that the non-linear moments aren’t detours. They’re often where the real development happens.

Steve Fretzin is a five-time bestselling author, host of the BE THAT LAWYER and Future Rainmakers podcasts, and a business development coach who works exclusively with attorneys. For more than 18 years, he has helped lawyers build strong books of business without selling, pitching, or chasing, using his proven Sales-Free Selling™ approach. His clients consistently become top rainmakers and credit his coaching and systems for driving meaningful, measurable growth. Steve can be reached directly at steve@fretzin.com, or through his website at www.bethatlawyer.com. Connect with him on LinkedIn at https://www.linkedin.com/in/stevefretzin. His ALL NEW BE THAT LAWYER Community is changing how lawyers develop the skills never taught in law school. Learn more at www.bethatlawyer.com/community.

articles.title: Niche Down To Blow Up: Micro-Specialization Marketing For Law Firms
articles.content:
Most of the time, “more is more” in law firm marketing: more blogs, higher word counts, maximal visibility. You will not often hear digital marketing professionals advocating the proverbial “less is more” approach. Occasionally, however, doing one thing better than anyone else can help you stand out from your competitors in a way that doing several things with moderate proficiency never could. If you are ready to “niche down” and offer a highly specialized set of services to a narrow-but-active client base, micro-specialization marketing may be your ticket to making “less is more” work for you.
You have more than likely encountered the concept of “niching down” many times before, whether you have ever considered the niche-marketing approach for your law firm or not. “Finding your niche” has become the go-to expression for a business strategy that focuses on identifying a narrow set of services at which you excel and building depth in that area (that niche), rather than trying to expand the range of services your law firm offers.
Marketing professionals also sometimes use “niche” to refer to the highly specialized industry or demographic your business aims to serve. A business strategy based on offering a limited range of high-quality specialized services tends to lend itself naturally to a tightly targeted marketing strategy based on finding and convincing the clients who appreciate a deep understanding of their needs and a demonstrated ability to provide exceptional results in the core set of services your business provides. The combination of a “niche-down” business model with a targeted approach to reaching and serving a niche market is what we call micro-specialization marketing.
Law can be a highly competitive profession, not just in the courtroom but when it comes to finding and retaining clients. Micro-specialization gives you the chance to become the absolute best at one thing, instead of “pretty good” at several. It also serves the function of immediately eliminating some of the “noise” that often makes audience targeting difficult in digital marketing campaigns.
You can think of niching down as targeting a specific type of legal service (e.g., only due diligence or only pre/postnuptial agreements), but if you are still developing your niche strategy then you may also want to consider offering more than one service, but tightly focused on a particular type of case or client need. Examples of niching down in this way might include offering services for every stage of international divorce, or support for franchising relationships. Without getting too far into business strategy (as opposed to marketing strategy), it’s a good idea to take a close look at how much local or statewide demand there is for a specific service across case types vs. a full range of legal services for a specific case type.
One of the strongest advantages of micro-specialization marketing is that addressing a very specific client need means your marketing team can target a very specific type of client. On social media and to a large extent in search as well, the more precise you can be about the kind of service a hypothetical client is looking for, the more easily you can assess the range of reasons why someone would be looking for that service. These reasons may not affect the structure of what you do with or for the client, once they are in your office, at all. In many cases, however, they do affect the specific searches that person decides to run. They may also give marketing professionals some insights into the “interests” social media platforms may be associating with the individual.
These interests will never be perfectly calibrated by social media algorithms, so they will never be perfectly targeted by marketing teams. On the other hand, you do not have to target every single interest a platform has identified for any given user for its algorithms to decide your posts are relevant; you only need to establish overlap. Search engine marketing can be even tighter, since you are working with queries that users themselves choose to enter. Selecting target keywords to align with the needs of a niche market gives you an edge over competitors who are targeting a broader audience to offer a more general service.
Most business advice is not really aimed at law firm growth (it hasn’t niched down!). That doesn’t mean you can’t use some of the same essential principles that apply to other types of businesses, but you may need to make some adaptations to ensure the implementation works for the specific conditions of your location and practice area.
One part of “niching down” is the work you do: the actual services your law firm performs, and the types of cases for which you offer them. Another aspect of niching down is made up of the clients you serve: the people (or entities) for whom you perform this work. Micro-specialization marketing sits at the intersection of the what and the who. As a general rule, this means your messaging will need to address the how and the why (the when is usually going to be determined initially by when a prospective client gives your law office a call, and by whatever procedural deadlines apply thereafter; you may not have to address the when at all, since normally it is a given).
Some of the most exciting potential of micro-specialization marketing for law firms comes from the degree to which it streamlines content strategy. What “content” looks like can vary widely from one industry to another, but law firms are ideally positioned to take advantage of digital audiences’ curiosity and desire for clear, actionable explanations of information directly relevant to their circumstances. Since prospective clients will be determining the searches they run and the kinds of content they seek out, as long as you (and your marketing team) have a solid understanding of what your ideal client’s circumstances are, you can design a content strategy around those conditions.
Often, this content strategy will involve more in-depth and detailed insights than you may be used to seeing on your competitors’ websites. There is nothing wrong with incorporating content with broad appeal, but when you understand a narrow market with exceptional depth, you can speak to legal strategies within your niche that are common concerns among your most likely clientele.
With a broader market, law firms generally stick to content that will be of interest to many, perhaps most, of the people who might need legal services in a practice area. Topics that will only have relevance for a small number of prospective clients get set aside as not having wide enough appeal. Niching down lets you take the opposite approach: You are no longer trying to appeal to as many people as possible, but rather trying to demonstrate expertise and understanding as deeply as possible for a much smaller group of people.
Some lesser-used outreach strategies, like podcast guesting, have their chance to truly shine in micro-specialization marketing. Webinars addressing specific sets of questions within your niche can also be highly effective, whether they are hosted by your law firm or you are contributing as a guest speaker to a webinar organized by an organization. Long-form articles and e-books explaining complex issues in your niche can be an excellent “hook” for clients in some areas. Talk with your digital marketing about possibilities for expanding your law firm digital marketing strategy by type of content, rather than venturing into topics outside your niche. In those discussions, be sure to keep your focus on your ideal client’s needs, so that you can frame your law firm’s approach to topics in terms of providing answers to questions people with those needs will likely have.
The wonderful thing about micro-specialization marketing for law firms is that this highly focused approach gives attorneys a chance to show the attention to detail and the depth of knowledge that are central to the quality of legal services you provide, but which can be hard to convey to a generalist audience. Showing that you understand potential clients’ questions and concerns, in a way that underscores how prepared your law firm is to directly address their needs, takes marketing from a crowded meet-and-greet to a quiet coffee chat. If you excel in a tightly focused area of law many of your competitors are not targeting, and you know exactly the kinds of clients who need those legal services, you are ready to develop a micro-specialization marketing strategy that builds a strong reputation and makes your law office the go-to firm for legal representation in your niche.
Annette Choti, Esq., has over two decades of legal experience and is the Founder & CEO of Law Quill, a concierge legal marketing agency for law firms. Annette authored the bestselling book Click Magnet: The Ultimate Guide To Digital Marketing For Law Firms, hosts the popular Legal Marketing Lounge podcast, and founded Click Magnet Academy where she teaches professionals to leverage the powerful LinkedIn platform. As a sought after speaker for Bar Associations, Legal Associations, and Marketing Conferences, Annette provides legal marketing insight along with an entertaining twist. Annette used to do theatre and professional comedy, which is not so different from the legal field if we are all being honest. Annette can be found on LinkedIn or directly through email at Annette@LawQuill.com

articles.title: How Appealing Weekly Roundup
articles.content:
**《上诉法院周度快讯》**

**1. 蒙大拿州提案禁止政治支出 涉及最高法院判决**
《纽约时报》记者尼尔·维格多尔报道，蒙大拿州的一项旨在限制企业政治捐款的措施将在11月投票中提上议程。反对者认为该法案违反了最高法院的裁决。

**2. 第九巡回上诉法庭推翻俄勒冈州收监变性女性的判决**
《法院新闻》记者希莱尔·阿龙报道，由特朗普任命的三名法官组成的合议庭批评了一位地方法官依赖“过时数据”和“毫无根据的猜测”，判决俄勒冈州不得将变性女性囚犯收押至女性监狱。

**3. 总检察长布兰奇的竞选活动打破了沃特门时代以来的伦理规范**
《纽约时报》记者查理·萨维奇分析指出，美国司法部长布兰奇为共和党的政治活动站台，加剧了司法部在沃特门事件后的价值观的恶化。

**4. 密苏里州选区划分听证会或引发最高法院新一轮审查**
《法院新闻》记者乔·哈里斯报道，密苏里州的选区划分案件可能再次被最高法院审查。该划分方案将给密苏里州共和党在7个国会席位中占优，民主党仅占1席。

**5. 巴雷特法官回避特朗普对最高法院的批评问题**
《彭博法律》记者霍莉·巴克尔和乔丹·费舍尔报道，巴雷特法官未对特朗普对最高法院的指责作出回应。

**6. 索托马约尔大法官担忧美国人可能无法“保住”共和制**
《塔尔萨世界报》记者兰迪·克雷比尔报道，索托马约尔大法官表示，她对美国人是否能维持共和制感到担忧。

（本文为《上诉法院周度快讯》的简要汇编，详细内容请参阅《How Appealing》博客）

“Blanche’s Political Campaigning Breaks an Ethical Norm Going Back to Watergate; The attorney general’s campaign politicking for Republicans adds to the degradation of post-Watergate values at the Justice Department”: Charlie Savage of The New York Times has this news analysis.

“Barrett Sidesteps Question About Trump Attacks on Supreme Court”: Holly Barker and Jordan Fischer of Bloomberg Law have this report.
